positions.stance: Full Medicaid expansion up to 138% of the poverty level as a day-one priority; end Pathways first and seek a higher federal match; opposes work requirements as unnecessary bureaucracy.
Argues leaving hundreds of thousands uninsured burdens local emergency rooms.

policyShifts.shift: Replace Pathways with full expansion; Georgia's current waiver expires in December and the next governor decides how coverage continues.

impediments.title: Federal work requirements
impediments.detail: Under the 2025 federal law, most expansion adults must show 80 hours of work a month; applies if Georgia expands, so her opposition cannot change the federal rule.

impediments.title: State cost unspecified
impediments.detail: Neither campaign detailed state costs; expansion needs legislative appropriation.

impediments.title: Pathways timeline
impediments.detail: CMS extended Pathways through at least end of 2026; the state requested a higher federal match.

impediments.title: Opponent's alternative
impediments.detail: Rick Jackson would pursue a state-designed waiver with work, education or training requirements.

insights: The federal work-requirement rule narrows the practical difference between her plan and the Republican one; the real fight is over the Pathways waiver that expires in December.
Because the waiver decision falls to the next governor at inauguration, the health-agency appointments (DCH, DPH) are early and high-stakes.
Legislative composition was not confirmed in sources opened; treat the Republican majority as likely but verify.
